The nose is not too impressive but undoubtedly will be ten times better in a couple of years (the wine is too young now), but there are lot of vanilla, strawberries (that seemed a little bit chemical) and chocolate on the palate, accompanied with beautifully balanced tannins and very long and mild finish. Aging potential promises to be extremely high and I hope the wine will seriously improve in a couple of years.

Now here we have an interesting wine.
As the name suggests it is made out of 5 indigenous grapes of mostly southern Italy ( Montepulciano, Sangiovese,Primitivo, Negroamaro   and Malvasia Nera) .
Dark purple color, expressive and baroque nose of lots of plum, prune, black cherry and sweet baking spices.
This is rather ostentatious.
On the palate soft and plush with velvety tannins but not flabby at all.
There is structure and lift with that very little sweetness on the finish.

5 grapes used (hence the name): Primitivo, Sangiovese, Negroamaro, Malvasia nera, Montepulciano.

Some dominant pepper on the nose and vanilla on the palate - but both will diminuish after a few minutes. Some sudden acidity on the finish that J didn’t appreciate so much.

A crowd pleaser (also keeps winning many prizes in Italy and elsewhere), but with no edges.

Wonderfully layered Italian blend. And a 99 pointer, too!

This Southern Italian multi-region Red blend is made up of Montepulciano, Primitivo, Sangiovese, Negroamaro and Malvasia. Separate vinification, inc 13m in 🇺🇸 and 🇫🇷 oak before blending.

Its rich and layered in texture. But soft too. The exotic nose and full bodied palate reveal intense blackberry, cherry and mulberry. A sure mid palate drive offers great contrast with sweet liquorice, cinnamon, dark chocolate and cedar oak spices. Great wine.

Excellent wine and one of the best Edizione I have tasted in recent years. This number 17 is a blend of several harvests. Made with 33% Montepulciano, 30% Primitivo, 25% Sangiovese, 7% Negroamaro and 5% Malvasia Nero. Aged for 13 months in French oak barrels. Aromas of raspberry, plum, blackberry, chocolate, tobacco, spices and vanilla. On the palate full bodied, structured, well balanced, good acidity. Polished tannins. Long and persistent finish. I recommend with great enthusiasm!!!

Foodpairing 27/10/2018 - closing wine 1
For closing an eveningwith some superb wines I picked one of my heaviest bottles.
It contains an unfiltered blend of montepulciano, primitivo, Sangiovese, negroamaro, malvasia with 13m oak.
N: superb nose. Blueberries, creamy, vanilla, coffee,...
Mounthfilling wine, warm, deep, layered, velvety. Fruity (oange), juicy and well seasoned (star anis). Beautiful acidity after the whole length.
17,5/20

Very good red blend made from Montepulciano 33%, Sangiovese 25%, Primitivo 30%, Malvasia Rossa 5%,
Negroamaro 7%. 14% of alchocol. Edizione is a dark ruby color, with an excellent aromatic complex dominated by intense fruity aromas of blackberry and cherry, enriched with notes of aromatic plants, cinnamon, carnation, cocoa and mineral touch. The palate shows an appropriate structure that is well balanced between the embrace of dictated by alcohol and adequate freshness. Tannins are soft and persistent. 4.2

Wonderful red blend from Abruzo and Puglia.
33% Montepulciano 30% Primitivo 25% Sangiovese 7% Negroamaro the rest Malvasia and Syrah.
Ezidione Cinque means "5 indigenous" grapes. This wine is made to prove Italian native grapes can produce amazing wine.
Very intense flavors of sugar plum,ripe dark cherry black tea and cacao powder dominate the palates followed by subtle smoky and spicy notes.
Super velvety tannins and jammy texture upfront with modest acidity.
Great right out of the bottle!!

It may be the golden 99pts. sticker on the neck but I'm definitely a fan of this wine. Last vintage tried was 2014 and was blown away but was still just learning about wine. A Capitol blend that is rounded but still can taste certain varietals. The primitivo notes lead to valpolicella body and the Sangiovese dried red flower finish.

The smell is pleasantly sweet, reminds me of black currant and perhaps even clean rubber. The colour is medium thick, almost light. After a few minutes in the glass some legs appear on the rims. The taste is subtle and smooth, after I swallow I feel some tannins on the tongue but without disturbing the balance. The taste also reminds me of black currant and maybe some leather.  The wine becomes better and better for every zip I take. I love this wine!

On the palate, it’s smooth, ‘softly spoken’ but bold with more black currant, compounded with blackberry and cherry with lovely sweet spice from the oak barrels. Finishes well with more vanilla and a touch of chocolate. Very easy drinking and perhaps a little young right now, but I have another bottle that I’ll leave for a couple of years (if I can 😉), as it’s lovely!

33% Montepulciano & 25% Sangiovese grown in Abruzzo with 30% Primitivo, 7% Negroamaro, 5% Malvasia Nera from southern Puglia. All grapes are separately vinified and matured (in 60% US & 40% French oak) before blending just before bottling. Most, but not all,of this comes from the ‘18 vintage.

Plenty of primary fruit (cherry and blackberry especially) with creamy vanilla too (but not a New World fruit bomb) but push beyond that and there’s clove, aniseed, cinnamon, cocoa, new leather and oak.

Soft, supple tannins lead to a long, drawn out finale !

A little lighter than I was expecting, but this was a seriously enjoyable bottle of wine. Beautiful chocolate aromas with hints of cherry when pouring, both of which follow through to the taste. An oaky backbone tempers the sweetness, as do darker fruit flavours of blackcurrant, bramble and plum. Very finely balanced tannins create interest, without that “sucking on a teabag” feeling you can get with some. Looking to extract every drop out of the bottle must be a good sign.

Interesting “Head2head” new vs old world as we had a bottle of “the Bird” lingering.
Surprised by the similarity between the Sangiovese and the 💤in. 💤abaco the more sophisticated, but such incredible £9 value for Curioso that it’s hard to beat! 
Similar raisin aromas and taste akin to Amarone due to air drying the grapes.

USA wins on absolute quality, Italy wins on absolute flavour for money - must be a score draw!

A very nice, fresh and fruity Primitivo with medium ruby appearance. Pronounced, very fruity nose of cherry, black cherry, fig, raisin, vanilla, jam.
Dry, medium acidity and tannins, high alcohol and full body. Pronounced flavor intensity, repeating the nose and adding some plum, licorice, chocolate, raisin sand walnut. Medium+ finish with aging potential.
Very good quality, nearly outstanding Primitivo and for just below 12 EUR, great value!
Cheers - Salud - Prost - Santé - Saúde

It tastes a little like a good primitivo at first, but that initial candy-chocolate-vanilla extract gives way to the barnyard mulch of monastrell. It's exactly what I find myself hoping primitivo will do, but too often it reaches it's logical conclusion of fruity sweetness (great for many other people, I know). Beautiful aubergine purple hue. Wonderful on the nose and that rich seam of vanilla, wow!

Primitivo di Manduria - key red wine of DOC of Puglia. Manduria is the cradle of Primitivo grape variety.
After grapes have been pressed, the juice ferments 20-30 days under controlled temperature. Aging 3-6 months in French oak.
The nose is expressive & rich with aromas of black cherry, black plum, cassis, licorice, sweet Christmas spices.
The palate is well balanced with medium tannins & medium + juicy acidity. Finish is rich with clove & cinnamon.

Drink it now, thank me later💋

Sweet and jammy. A very mild and pleasant merlot. Blueberry and strawberry but ends with a spicy and dry finale.

Intriguing cherry, wintergreen, maple syrup, orange glaze, on the nose.  Grippy, resinous tannins & earthy, sour cherry, blackberry notes teeter on a see saw back and forth, with brighter & lighter lemoncello & yellow plum, apricot notes.  Like Schrödinger’s cat, seems to land at 2 different places at once, depending on when the box, or the bottle, is opened.  Mystery leads to interesting, but ultimately, discordant drama.
